_: Bounds the compare table is held to. All three are absolute limits: 'median' caps the magnitude of the signed median, 'abs_median' caps the median absolute error, which is the one that can fail when errors of opposite sign cancel, and 'p90' caps the 90th percentile of that absolute error, which is the one that can fail when a minority of rows is far out and the median is not. A dimension can sit inside both medians while nearly half its rows are outside the references' own spread. 'rows' is how many of the grid's rows survived censoring into that median, so a later run can tell whether it is comparing against the same population. Re-record only in the same change as the behaviour that justifies it.
_rerecorded: attack_hf (median 1.0 -> 14.338) and balance (median 0.725 -> 2.22) moved with the voice change that gave the harp its upper partials: under the previous 0.07 s hf_decay_s the model's h3-h5 fell at 50-270 dB/s, so inside the 0.12-1.62 s window the partial stack and the 4-8 kHz share were measured on partials that had already died and matched the reference by that accident. Both bounds now describe partials that sound. Deleted by hand before re-recording, since _keep_the_tighter would otherwise have held the accidental values.

_excluded.body: below f0 the reference carries the source's own gain modulation rather than a body: at 7 of 9 notes the energy the metric reads is one line at f0 minus 125 or 250 Hz (-50 to -58 dB re the fundamental), the lower sideband of a gain update every 8 ms that every partial carries, and at note 48 a 50 Hz hum line (-67.8 dB). Notching those lines moves the reading from -50/-55 to -57…-80 dB; they sit at no harp string's pitch and at no fixed frequency (60-273 Hz across the grid)
_excluded.tnr: everything the metric counts as noise in the reference is modulation sidebands of the partials - 100 % of the non-tonal power lies below 1 kHz, in lines at f0 +- 5 Hz (-36 to -44 dB, a 5.0 Hz amplitude modulation at every note) and at n*f0 + k*125 Hz (-52 to -58 dB). Against the recordings' real floor (-93 to -105 dB per bin) the ratio would read 71-78 dB, not the 35-50 recorded, so a bound here would hold the model to the source's synthesis
